source_map.note: header names of the per-series tables (Compare 50/40/30/20/16 Series Specs); s24 gives the PCI-ID product names, the only official list for Pascal (GTX 10)
no segment field anywhere; a card on the desktop graphics-cards compare page is taken as desktop. Laptop parts are on a separate page (not opened)

summary table row 'Architecture Name Blackwell Ada Lovelace Ampere Turing Turing Pascal' (columns RTX 50, 40, 30, 20, GTX 16, GTX 10); per-series tables rows 'NVIDIA Architecture' (40, 30), 'NVIDIA Architecture Name' (20, 16), 'Shader Cores' (50)

no NVIDIA spec page carries a date. NVIDIA dated news posts: s15 (RTX 3060, 2021-02-25), s13 (RTX 4060, June 2023), s17 (GTX 1080 Ti, on sale March 10th). All other dates from Wikipedia tables (official false)

Linux driver README Appendix A, one flat table 'name | PCI ID | class'; latest.txt at download.nvidia.com/XFree86/Linux-x86_64/latest.txt gives the newest version. README does not mark desktop vs laptop nor memory size, so ids of every row with the plain name are listed
row 'Standard Memory Config' per series table ('A / B' cells for two variants: 2060, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3080, 4070, 5060 Ti). Pascal: no official page found except 1080 Ti (s16)
same cell as size
row 'Memory Interface Width' (50 to 16 series tables). Pascal: none (Wikipedia s26, official false)
NVIDIA states no data rate per card; 50 series derivable from its bandwidth and bus rows. Else Wikipedia 'Memory (MT/s)' or '(Gb/s)' columns, official false
only the 50 series table has the row 'Memory Bandwidth'. Else Wikipedia, official false (merged cells in its tables noted per cell)
row 'NVIDIA CUDA® Cores' per series table; 1080 Ti s16; other Pascal: no official page | Pascal except 1080 Ti: Wikipedia GeForce 10 series (s26), official false

row 'Boost Clock (GHz)' (50 to 20 series) or 'Boost Clock (MHz)' (16 series); the table says clocks apply to the Founders Edition or reference design | Pascal except 1080 Ti: Wikipedia GeForce 10 series (s26), official false
only the 40 series table, row 'Shader Cores' ('Ada Lovelace 15 TFLOPS'); it does not say FP32 in words. Else Wikipedia, official false
row 'Tensor Cores' / 'Tensor Cores (AI)' with generation; '-' for GTX 16 and GTX 10

all architectures: CUDA Programming Guide Table 36 (s4), read with page.py --table: header FP64 TF32 BF16 FP16 FP8 FP6 FP4 INT8 INT4, rows 7.5, 8.6, 8.9, 12.x; empty cells are collapsed so Yes cells are assigned left to right. Cross-checked with the Turing (s6) and Ampere (s7) tuning guides
PTX ISA dp4a: 'Requires sm_61 or higher.' (compute capability 6.1). The CUDA Math API page (docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-math-api, group CUDA_MATH_INTRINSIC_INT) lists __dp4a but gives no minimum
CUDA 12.9 programming guide Table 7 'Throughput of Native Arithmetic Instructions', row '16-bit floating-point add, multiply, multiply-add' (6.1, 7.x, 8.6, 8.9 readable; 12.0 not separable)
summary table row 'CUDA Capability 12.0 8.9 8.6 7.5 7.5 6.1' (columns RTX 50, 40, 30, 20, GTX 16, GTX 10) and the per-series rows. s1 lists only GTX 1650 Ti for GTX 16
summary table row 'Vulkan 1.4 1.4 1.4 1.4 1.4 1.4' (all six columns incl. GTX 10); s9 says Vulkan 1.4 for Blackwell, Ada, Ampere and Turing
one generic sentence: OpenCL 3.0 conformant on R465 and later drivers; no per-GPU list
